innervation.root_levels: T7-T12 (thoracoabdominal + subcostal nerves, one segment innervated per tendinous-intersection compartment)

actions: compresses abdominal contents / raises intra-abdominal pressure

functional_compartments.name: Segment 1 (superior, costal)
functional_compartments.function_note: Most cranial of the muscle's tendinous-intersection-bounded segments; a textbook example of a single named muscle subdivided into separately-innervated, individually-contractile compartments.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Segment 2
functional_compartments.function_note: Second segment, bounded above and below by tendinous intersections that adhere firmly to the anterior rectus sheath.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Segment 3
functional_compartments.function_note: Third segment, roughly at the level of the umbilicus.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Segment 4 (inferior, pubic)
functional_compartments.function_note: Longest, most caudal segment (intersections are not present below the umbilicus in most individuals) running to the pubic attachment.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Longitudinal or transverse, paramedian, anywhere between the costal margin and the pubis -- most conveniently at the point of maximum thickness, typically just above the umbilicus.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Within the rectus sheath: anterior sheath superficial, posterior sheath deep (absent below the arcuate line, where the muscle lies directly on transversalis fascia and peritoneum).
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Paired vertical straps flanking the linea alba, crossed by hyperechoic tendinous intersections; contracts on a head-and-shoulders-raise maneuver.
structures_at_risk: superior and inferior epigastric vessels, running within the sheath on the muscle's deep surface
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A target for chronic abdominal wall myofascial pain, and, alongside the lateral wall muscles, for preoperative botulinum toxin ('chemical component separation') before complex ventral hernia repair -- reduces fascial tension and lets more hernias close primarily.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Quevedo-Cruz D et al., Hernia 30:75 (2026), doi:10.1007/s10029-025-03558-7 -- ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin prehabilitation technique for complex ventral hernia (PubMed); Zamkowski M et al., Pol Przegl Chir 97(6):1 (2025), doi:10.5604/01.3001.0055.3078 -- volumetric muscle elongation by layer after lateral wall injection (PubMed)

trigger_points.location_description: Upper trigger points in the rectus abdominis, above the umbilicus, including a point near the xiphoid process.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain referred horizontally across the mid-back at the thoracolumbar junction ('bra-line' pain), and, from the point near the xiphoid, pain and tenderness across the upper abdomen with symptoms that can mimic heartburn/indigestion (nausea, belching, epigastric fullness).
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Direct abdominal trauma or surgical scarring, chronic coughing, and postural overload from prolonged sitting in a slumped position.
trigger_points.notes: The abdominal-cramping/heartburn-mimicking referral of upper rectus abdominis trigger points is a classically cited example of a myofascial trigger point being mistaken for visceral disease.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (2nd ed. 1999, Vol 1), rectus abdominis chapter, as reflected in secondary clinical compilations (Morningside Acupuncture NYC and TriggerPointTherapist.com rectus abdominis references); general finding of rectus abdominis trigger points in abdominal wall pain corroborated by Rajkannan P, Vijayaraghavan R (2018) "Dry needling in chronic abdominal wall pain of uncertain origin." J Bodyw Mov Ther 23(1):94-98, doi:10.1016/j.jbmt.2018.01.004, PMID 30691770 (PubMed).

trigger_points.location_description: Lower trigger points in the rectus abdominis, between the umbilicus and the pubis.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain referred horizontally across the low back at belt-line level and into both sacroiliac joints, and -- clinically important in women -- a lower rectus abdominis trigger point pattern that reproduces cramping menstrual-type pain (dysmenorrhea).
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Abdominal surgery/scarring (e.g. Cesarean section), chronic straining, and the same cyclic pelvic nociceptive input implicated in primary dysmenorrhea.
trigger_points.notes: A 1983 Simons & Travell paper specifically describes lower rectus abdominis trigger points referring pain horizontally across the low back; the dysmenorrhea association has since been supported by controlled quantitative sensory testing.
trigger_points.source: Simons DG, Travell JG (1983) "Myofascial origins of low back pain. 2. Torso muscles." Postgrad Med 73(2):81-92, doi:10.1080/00325481.1983.11697757, PMID 6218490 (PubMed) -- lower rectus abdominis trigger points refer pain horizontally across the low back; Hoyos-Calderon YT et al. (2022) "Myofascial Trigger Points and Central Sensitization Signs, but No Anxiety, Are Shown in Women with Dysmenorrhea: A Case-Control Study." Biology (Basel) 11(11):1550, doi:10.3390/biology11111550, PMID 36358253, PMC9688021 (PubMed) -- case-control study finding hyperalgesic rectus abdominis trigger points and lower pressure-pain thresholds in women with primary dysmenorrhea; Temel MH, Bagcier F (2023) "Abdominal Wall Pain and Primary Dysmenorrhea: The Importance of Myofascial Trigger Points." Complement Med Res 30(4):360-361, doi:10.1159/000530035, PMID 36893743 (PubMed).

trigger_points.location_description: A lateral trigger point in the lower rectus abdominis, near the muscle's lateral border, on the right side in the same location as (and mimicking) McBurney's point.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Localized tenderness and referred pain in the same lower abdominal quadrant; on the right side this pattern has specifically been reported to mimic the pain of appendicitis.
trigger_points.notes: A cited example of myofascial pain masquerading as an acute abdominal/surgical condition -- relevant to differential diagnosis before pursuing invasive workup for right lower quadrant pain.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (2nd ed. 1999, Vol 1), rectus abdominis chapter, as reflected in secondary clinical compilations (TriggerPointTherapist.com rectus abdominis reference).
